set_text.text: Accounts receivable turnover counts how many times a year your customers pay off what they owe you. You get it by dividing credit sales by the average amount owed. Turned into days, it shows how long an invoice really takes to become cash.
A book turning 9.4 times a year can still hold a debt that will never be paid. The ratio measures speed, not the risk in any one account.
The ratio blends every customer, so the 8.8 days past terms could sit with one account or with all of them. An aging report by account shows which.
You collect from accounts in 38.8 days, and that clock only starts once a case sells. Every day between paying your supplier and getting paid is cash you fund yourself.
Who uses an accounts receivable turnover calculator
It is for independent food distributors who sell to accounts on credit. Anyone who sets terms, grants credit or answers to a lender about cash should know the number.
